entry.title: Summer Self-Propelled, by Kyle Richardson
entry.content:
Kyle Richardson— is a force to be wreckoned with: elite mountain runner, endurance athlete, and the newest addition to our Moots ambassador family. Known for his speed on foot and deep connection to the terrain under his shoes, Kyle brings the same energy, focus, and love for the long haul to two wheels. As he expands his adventures beyond trail running and into the world of titanium, we’re proud to welcome him to the Moots crew. This partnership is all about shared passion—for movement, for the mountains, and for the pursuit of pure performance.

----

The adventure is simple: start from your front door, travel under your own power to a compelling destination, have an experience, and return. There are many tools for traveling in the mountains. Instinctively, my background as a runner compels me to seek things out on foot—getting a closer look at a place by running through the terrain. It’s intimate and personal, feeling the rocks and landscape underfoot.

But what if you could expand on that experience and feel the full spectrum of mountain movement? Insert the bike.

[caption id="attachment_53559" align="aligncenter" width="767"]Processed with VSCO with k1 preset[/caption]

Traveling on two wheels introduces a new element: a clean, efficient, logical, and beautiful way to move from the bottom of the foothills to the summits of peaks—experiencing everything the area has to offer. It’s a multi-disciplinary mountain style where endurance, technique, and vision unlock new ways around a landscape. It’s not about the fastest way, but the most aesthetic and challenging route. In return, you’re rewarded with a comprehensive and fulfilling day out in the hills. Don’t ask me about watts or numbers—I’m here for the experience, the surfaces, the views, and the reward of traveling somewhere untethered and free.

From my front doorstep in Boulder, we have access to the Continental Divide, some 20 to 30 miles away. This alluring stretch of jagged, inspiring peaks has been my stomping ground for the past decade. I certainly haven’t climbed every peak in the area, but I’ve spent enough time there to feel familiar and comfortable. Introducing the bike as a means of transportation to the trailheads has opened up a new level of efficiency. I’ve started to think outside the box—searching for new ways to link up these different mountains right from my doorstep. It’s an ongoing project, or maybe just a lifestyle. By no means do I have it figured out. There are no rules—just the idea of doing it yourself.

[caption id="attachment_53560" align="aligncenter" width="768"]Processed with VSCO with ss1 preset[/caption]

The setup is pretty simple: strap your running shoes to your handlebars, toss in some snacks and a water filter, and start pedaling. No matter where you live—big city or small village—I believe it’s universal that there’s something worth exploring in your own backyard. It might take some creativity, but there’s probably something tall, historical, or interesting to go check out.

I’m inspired to take the road less traveled—to get off the tarmac and onto technical backroads. This is where the Moots Routt ESC really shines. At its core, it’s an adventure bike—capable on any surface or terrain. Having a tool like this is critical for me; it supports the vision I have for these big mountain days.

[caption id="attachment_53556" align="aligncenter" width="768"]Processed with VSCO with ss1 preset[/caption]

In Boulder, we’re fortunate to have every style of road and riding imaginable. Want smooth and fast pavement in the mountains? Ride up Lefthand Canyon to Brainard Lake. Looking for rough, chunky, gnarly riding? Go up Kingston Peak or Rollins Pass. Gravel? No problem—head up Fourmile Canyon to Gold Hill.The point is, there’s a full spectrum of terrain. That makes route planning both exciting and challenging. It’s part of the fun—digging into the maps, linking together routes, and exploring every nook and cranny of my backyard. The bike unlocks a new way to travel. Having a bike that can handle anything lets me focus on the movement itself. Instead of worrying about gear or setup, I’m free to dive deep into the experience and feel everything the landscape has to offer. It helps that the titanium frame makes all the rough stuff feel like smooth butter, yet stiff and responsive enough for all the climbing at hand. When you boil it down, for me I go uphill for a long time, I need a bike that climbs really well, the Routt ESC checks that box! So light and snappy. It is an absolute joy to pedal.

This self-propelled way of travel is romantic. Sure, I still use a car now and then. The point of this isn’t to make anyone feel bad about driving to the trailhead. It’s about showcasing the beauty and style of creating your own adventures—right from your doorstep.The bike is the ultimate freedom tool and a perfect companion for long days in the mountains. It opens new pathways of movement, and when paired with a run or a hike, it just might open your eyes to a whole new kind of adventure.

Happy summer—hope you’re enjoying your trails, mountains, and open spaces!

Kyle Richardson

You can read more about Kyle's adventures on his substack: https://substack.com/home/post/p-158319612)KR Self

entry.title: Rider Spotlight: Mark DeLeon & Mely
entry.content:
For Mark DeLeon, it was love at first sight — a gold-accented Vamoots RSL whose flawless welds spoke of true craftsmanship. Named Mely after his grandmother, this bike is a tribute to resilience, strength, and grace.

From city alleys to the Singapore Criterium, Mark rides with intention: “Not to impress, but to express myself.” Three words sum it up: Timeless. Craftsmanship. Resilient.

---

What originally drew you to Moots? Was it the craftsmanship, the ride feel, the titanium, or something else?

The titanium caught my attention with its anodized detailing is perfect. I did check the brand out and saw how its built and precisely crafted; thats when I knew I found my forever bike.

 

Why did you pick your model bike?  

I bought it through a friend which collects Moots and the bike really has an appeal to me. love at first sight. I look on bike aesthetically and with that gold accent makes it better. Im a big fan of rim break so having it in the bike works perfectly.

 

Are there any details of the bike you are obsessed with? 

Definitely the welds. Every time I look closely, im reminded that this frame was built by hand not in a factory.

Did you customize the build? Did you build this with a local shop, if so, which? 

I got the bike already setup. I just switch some parts and want to have modern component in it. Its built full enve and i’ll keep it that way.

 

Any standout adventures, races, or moments that made you think, “This is why I bought this bike”? 

We got invited to participate in the singapore criterium last November 2024 and I used it in the race. Using it in the street exploring singapore knowing how versatile titanium is gives me peace of mind and security that whatever happens I have a trusted bike.

What does riding a Moots mean to you? 

Riding in moots means riding with intention, not to impress but to express myself as a cyclist. I respect the craftsmanship put in the build of every bike and riding it is a work of art.

What terrain or type of ride do you do the most on your Moots?

I love city rides, cruising and discovering hidden alleys from the beach to the track theres a lot of spots you can discover and makes every ride unique.

 

Tell us about a memorable ride, or trip that you took with your Moots.

The most memorable ride I had with my moots was in singapore where we did an alley cat race, its like having a city tour on a bike. Checking out key destination spot in singapore early in the morning with friends is by far the best experience I had.

 

If you had to describe your bike in three words, what would they be?

  • timeless
  • craftsmanship
  • resilient

Did you buy your bike from a shop, if so what is the shop's name?

I bought it from a close friend who also collects Moots in Abu Dhabi. shout out to Cromwell!!!

 

If this bike had a name or personality, what would it be?

I named my moots after my grandmother - mely. Her resilience, strenght and grace continues to inspire me everyday. She taught me the value of patience, of doing things the right way, and of carrying yourself with quiet pride, all qualities I see in this bike. It’s more than just a bike; it’s a reflection of where I come from and who shaped me.

Tell us about your bike build! 

  • my moots is a vamoots rsl with gold accent
  • carbon ti chain ring
  • srm power meter
  • enve wheelset
  • enve seatpost
  • enve cockpit
  • sram red
  • chris king headset
  • ceramic speed bottom bracket

 

Mark DeLeon’s gold-accented Vamoots RSL was love at first sight — a masterpiece of titanium craftsmanship named Mely in honor of his grandmother. From city streets to the Singapore Criterium, it’s carried him through adventures with unmatched trust and style. We thank Mark for sharing his passion for Moots with us — riding not to impress, but to express.

entry.title: MADE 2025: Wrap-Up
entry.content:
What a weekend. The energy at MADE in Portland was incredible, and we couldn’t be more grateful to everyone who stopped by our booth, shared stories, and celebrated titanium with us. To all of our loyal fans, friends, and new faces—thank you for making this show such a success.

This year, we brought a lineup of bikes that each told a different story of what titanium can do.

Adventure Bike, New Model Preview

Purpose-built for big days out, this new adventure platform showed off progressive geometry, tons of mounts, and internal routing—all wrapped in a topo-inspired anodized finish. It’s our vision for the next era of all-surface exploration. More information avaliable this fall.

 

Routt 45 “City Slicker”

A one-off concept that turned heads at the Shimano booth. Outfitted with Shimano’s new Q’Auto electronic drivetrain, flat bars, custom Sims fenders, and our new CRD Bearing Cap, the City Slicker reimagines a Routt 45 as a sleek, titanium commuter.

Routt CRD Blackbird

Handcrafted in Steamboat Springs and handpainted in Portland, the Blackbird was our ultimate showpiece. This size 55 one-of-one made its final appearance at MADE before being offered for sale—a true collector’s piece of Moots history. If you are interested in purchasing this bike, please inquire with info@moots.com

 

Womble 29, Cerakote Lavender

Our playful titanium hardtail, shown in a bold lavender Cerakote finish with an MRP Ribbon SL Rally fork. Updated with a double-butted front triangle, UDH dropouts, and optional sliders, the Womble proved just how versatile and modern a titanium MTB can be.

Each bike we presented reflected our constant pursuit of craftsmanship, performance, and timeless design. Remeber...NO COMPROMISES!

The conversations, the rides, and the stoke from MADE remind us why we do what we do. Events like this are about more than bikes—they’re about community. Thank you for being part of ours.

Until next time.

entry.title: Kyle Richardson’s North East Summits Route Preparation
entry.content:
Adventure means something different to Kyle Richardson. This September, he’s setting out on the North East Summits Route—a 20-day, self-supported bike-to-run journey from New York City to New Hampshire. With a Moots Routt ESCas his companion, Kyle is chasing discovery across pavement, singletrack, and summits.

---

Wilco’s Yankee Hotel Foxtrot spins on vinyl, filling Kyle’s studio with a relaxed, methodical energy as I find him amidst last-minute trip preparations. He’s headed east for a bike-to-run tour—one he devised as an expression of his intrinsic drive to explore mountain ranges under his own power. When I asked Kyle what it’s all about, he replied simply. “Distill things down. What do you need to travel self-supported? Load that on your bike, toss in your running shoes, and off you go. Find an objective that inspires you, and commit to the journey.” Starting from New York City, Kyle will aim for New Hampshire by way of a series of running and climbing objectives. All told, he’ll spend about 20 days out. “NES or North East Summits is a route that follows the greater Northern Appalachian mountains. From the biggest city to the tallest summits, the inspiration and motivation lies in exploring the in-between spaces of some of the world’s oldest mountains.” Kyle’s riding the MOOTS Routt ESC for its mix of long-range comfort and readiness to handle the unexpected. The terrain will shift between forgotten doubletrack, winding singletrack, and quiet stretches of rolling pavement. Everything fits on the bike—no pack required. Feathers in the seat bag, running shoes in the handlebar roll, tent/tools/water/food in the frame bag. Navigation runs through Gaia GPS, with a solar-powered Garmin Enduro watch logging the journey. We roll the bike outside for a final check. Kyle steps back, admiring the refined setup. I can tell he’s both anxious and eager—ready for the full immersion in discovery.

• MOOTS Routt ESC

• 2.4 Maxxis Ikon tires

• Chris King carbon wheelset

• SRAM AXS drivetrain

• White Industries Crankset

• ENVE Adventure Bars

• Brooks C15 Saddle

• Custom frame bag by Thomas Woodson

Follow his adventure through September at: instagram.com/kylerichardson

 

Written by Thomas Woodson

entry.title: Lauren Hall: Summer Miles, New Friends, and Giving Back
entry.content:
First, a quick apology for the late post-the end of June and start of July had me sidelined with COVID, and for two solid weeks there was zero exercise of any kind. Once I was back on my feet, though, the summer cycling calendar hit full speed, and I've been soaking up every mile and every moment since.
 
In July, the team and I hosted the USA Cycling Foundation's annual Tour de France Femmes trip, a tradition we plan for our major supporters. Not just to watch, but to truly experience it - riding up the legendary Cols before the pros arrived, feeling the crowd's roar echo off the mountains, and sharing those moments with an incredible group who believe in supporting the next generation of cyclists and women's cycling! These trips mean so much to me.
From the French Alps, I swapped tarmac for dirt and headed to the Leadville 100 - this time with a microphone instead of a number plate. I had the privilege of commentating for the Life Time Grand Prix series, which gave me a front-row seat to the grit, dust, and determination that make Leadville legendary. Being there to call the action while cheering on my gravel family was such a great weekend.
 
 
And now, I'm closing out the season by hosting an athlete at my home - a small way to give back after so many people opened their doors, their wisdom, and their hearts to me during my own racing career. Watching the next generation chase their dreams reminds me why I fell in love with the sport in the first place.
 
Cycling has always been about more than the miles. It's about the stories we share, the roads we ride together, and the way we lift each other up along the way. This summer has been full of all three - and I wouldn't trade it for anything.
 
Next up, USA Cycling Foundation event in Aspen, CO - August 21st, followed by commentating Chequamegon in September!
 
-Lauren Hall

entry.title: Moots: In Me, the Tiger Sniffs the Rose
entry.content:
From the moment Mr. Duan first saw a Moots outside Tsinghua University in Beijing, to riding thousands of miles on Vamoots and Routt models across Asia and beyond, Moots has been a lifelong companion. Through Granfondos, long tours, and even the challenges of the pandemic, each bike has carried him with strength, beauty, and endurance. For him, Moots is more than a bike—it’s a reminder that the journey itself is the reward.

---

 

Whenever a friend with a generous budget asks me to recommend the ultimate metal bike, my answer is always the same—Moots. It has been my favorite brand for as long as I can remember. With cycling at the heart of my life for over 20 years, I have owned—and still cherish—five different Moots bikes: Vamoots, Vamoots RSL, Routt RSL, Vamoots CRD, and Routt CRD. My love for bicycles is lifelong, and I am certain that no other brand will ever surpass the place Moots holds in my heart.

My journey with Moots began in 2007, during my university years, when high-performance sports bikes were still a rare sight in mainland China. Near the entrance of Tsinghua University in Beijing, a well-known bike shop had a Moots on display. The moment I saw it, I froze—it was unlike anything I had ever encountered. At the time, titanium frames were a niche choice, embraced only by a small group of devoted enthusiasts. A masterpiece like Moots, with its flawless craftsmanship, felt almost unattainable—proud, exclusive, and reserved for the few. As a university student surviving on a modest monthly allowance of less than $100, owning a Moots YBB seemed like a distant dream. Yet, that bike left an indelible mark on me—much like an ancient Chinese verse describing the love for the Lotus: a thing of beauty to be admired from afar, untouchable in its grace.

Years later, my dream came true. For my 28th birthday in 2017, my girlfriend—now my wife—surprised me with my first Moots: a Vamoots from Taiwan Province. Although it wasn’t the brand’s top-tier model, it still showcased Moots' hallmark precision welding, timeless design, and exceptional ride quality. I was captivated. I would admire it at home, take it out for a ride whenever I could, and savor every moment in the saddle.

I find it hard to put into words the unforgettable riding experience: stiff yet comfortable, soft as cotton yet as fast as lightning. From that moment on, Moots became my unwavering companion. When AITASHOP started collaborating with Moots to bring these masterpieces to Chinese cyclists, I was overjoyed. They introduced me to my first top-tier model, the Vamoots RSL, featuring custom geometry and breathtaking anodized details—a dream realized.

That bike has been with me through countless adventures, including all six stages and 8,400 meters of climbing at the Granfondo Yunnan in 2019, as well as a 1,000km tour through southern Sichuan. The magic of a Moots titanium frame lies in its unique ability to combine endurance with racing performance—a rare blend. Among all my road bikes, the Vamoots RSL still holds the highest mileage. Wherever I go, it is my soul companion, giving me the confidence to tackle long distances, remote roads, and challenging climbs.

As the popularity of gravel riding grew, I built up a Routt RSL to embrace the new discipline. This bike became my sanctuary during the challenging days of COVID-19, when physical and mental struggles affected us all. It carried me through villages, towns, and open fields, offering new perspectives on roads I thought I knew.

Later, when the CRD series was introduced, I knew I had to experience them, Vamoots CRD and Routt CRD, both of them. With its fully integrated system, MOD components, and new geometry. The Vamoots CRD immediately stood out—particularly its flatter top tube, which improved both compatibility and ride feel. I spent a lot of time carefully selecting each component to ensure a perfect build. Now, for any ride over 120km, the Vamoots CRD is my only choice.

Oh, I almost forgot—Granfondo Yunnan 2024. Despite some unexpected challenges, I am even more grateful for my Vamoots CRD, a bike that now holds even deeper personal significance. Looking ahead to the next five years, I wonder—will anything else accompany me during those defining moments, as the Vamoots RSL did before?

As I reflect on my journey with Moots, I realize that no matter how much time passes or how the market changes, Moots will always be my favourite. Like a steady companion on a lifelong ride, it has been with me through countless miles, challenges, and triumphs. As the saying goes, "The journey is the reward", and every ride on a Moots serves as a reminder of that truth. With each new chapter in life, I look forward to the next chapter in Moots' evolution—because, just like my passion for cycling, it’s a ride that will never end.

Mr. Duan

entry.title: From Residency to Routt RSL: A Ride Worth the Reward
entry.content:
Photo by Ethan Herrold

 

For some, a bike is just a tool. For others, it’s a milestone—a symbol of where they’ve been, and where they’re going. After completing medical residency, Dr. Emily gifted herself something extraordinary: a handcrafted titanium machine built for freedom, self-care, and serious fun. In this Q&A, we dive into why she chose the Routt RSL, how the custom build came together, and why this bike—equal parts art and performance—continues to inspire her both on the trail and in the clinic.

 

What originally drew you to Moots? Was it the craftsmanship, the ride feel, the titanium, or something else?

I learned about Moots from Alpha Bicycle Studio and fell in love with the high quality, their Colorado heritage, and the art like details on their bikes. I wanted a sturdy bike that was comfortable, beautiful and well-crafted.

Why did you pick the Routt RSL?

I chose Routt RS as I wanted a fast, fun and playful gravel bike that could tackle over biking on single track but still be agile enough for riding on the road.

 

How did you decide on the finish or anodization? Are there any details of the bike you are obsessed with?

I chose the Stanley finish as I am an artist. I love the color and detail, especially on the chain stay. I also love Estes Park and the Stanley hotel; we go annually and always come to the Stanley.

 

Did you customize the build? Did you build this with a local shop, if so, which?

I customized the build with Alpha Bicycle Studio in Littleton. They completed a bike fit prior to the build, recommended sizes and coordinated with me on each aspect of the build.

 

 

Any standout adventures, races, or moments that made you think, “This is why I bought this bike”?

I race Foco Fondo yearly and completed the blue course at SBT GRVL last year. The bike always turns heads, but I really love the bike on gnarly gravel descents where I feel comfortable, fast and confident that my Moots can handle it all.

 

What does riding a Moots mean to you?

Moots means expert craftsmanship that blends function and fun.

If you had to describe your bike in three words, what would they be?

I describe my bike as a piece of art, reliable and a beast!

 
Photo by Ethan Herrold

I purchased my Moots after finishing medical residency, the bike represents an ultimate self-care gift and the beginning of freedom to enjoy outside hobbies. I now work as a primary care physician and medical director. I use my moots to clear my head after long days caring for patients. I often bond with patients on cycling and always push for patients to get outside and move!

entry.title: RANCH RALLY 2025: A CELEBRATION OF GRAVEL, COMMUNITY, AND HERITAGE
entry.content:
Event Date: Saturday, July 26th, 2025Location: Steamboat Springs, Colorado

Well howdy, partner! We’re mighty excited to invite y’all to the Moots Ranch Rally 2025, a one-of-a-kind gravel cycling event that brings together world-class riding, Western roots, and a whole lotta heart. This year’s route rolls right out our front doors here in Steamboat Springs, covering the same gravel roads and sweeping mountain views that have inspired our work at Moots Cycles for over four decades. Whether you’re a seasoned gravel grinder or a newcomer to backroad bliss, this is a ride built for connection — to the land, the bike, and the community.

Gravel Riding, Steamboat Style

Home to the well known SBT Gravel and tucked in the heart of Colorado's Yampa Valley, Steamboat Springs is a gravel riding paradise. Known for its expansive ranch lands, alpine vistas, and smooth-as-butter dirt roads, this area offers some of the finest and most scenic gravel routes in the country. The Ranch Rally is built on these very roads — not just as a course, but as a tribute. Riders will pedal through open landscapes framed by the Flat Tops, past working ranches, aspen groves, and winding rivers, all while enjoying the kind of serene solitude and unspoiled terrain that makes gravel riding so special.

BUCKAROO ROUTE

39 miles | 2,500 ft of climbing. View the route: [Click here to see on RidewithGPS]

Expect a well-marked course, support vehicles, and roaming medical assistance to keep everyone safe and smiling. This is a non-competitive ride, so leave the race face at home and come ride for the experience.

 

 

40 Years of Moots Magic

Since 1981, Moots has been hand-building titanium bikes right here in Steamboat Springs. Our shop is more than a factory — it’s a workshop of passion, precision, and purpose. For over 40 years, we've been crafting bikes that reflect this place: durable, elegant, and built to ride for a lifetime. Hosting the Ranch Rally on our home turf is more than just convenient — it’s personal. These are the roads that shaped our bikes, and this event is our way of sharing that magic with you. Whether you’re rollin’ in on a Moots or just curious about what makes this place so special, the Ranch Rally is more than just a ride — it’s a celebration. Of gravel. Of craftsmanship. Of community. And of the Colorado ranching spirit that grounds us all.

Rooted in Ranching

The Ranch Rally isn’t just a ride — it’s a community fundraiser that supports the Community Agriculture Alliance (CAA), a local nonprofit dedicated to preserving and promoting the agricultural heritage of the Yampa Valley. This land has been cared for by ranching families for generations, and their stewardship has helped preserve the open spaces we ride through today. We’re proud to partner with the CAA to honor that legacy and help keep our community connected to the food and land that sustains it.

 

Spots are limited to just 200 riders, so grab your spot before they’re gone.

Each rider gets:✔️ Limited edition Ranch Rally swag✔️ A spot on the ride with aid station support✔️ Post-ride lunch at Moots HQ✔️ Western-style cookout with local ranch fare, cold beverages, live music✔️ Raffle entry for a Moots Routt gravel frame

Click here to register: 2025 Ranch Rally Registration

Rain or shine, we ride. See y’all out there.

entry.title: Travel Light, Ride Hard: My Moots on the Move
entry.content:
From the moment I picked up my Moots, I knew it was special. The titanium frame is not just beautiful -it’s durable, reliable, and can take a beating from TSA without flinching. Whether I’m packing it into a bike bag for a cross-country flight or tossing it on the bike rack on my truck for a road trip, I never worry about it showing up on the other side worse for wear.

My go-to bike bag is the Scion Sports Aerocomfort bike bag. When I pack my bike into the bike bag, I remove the pedals, take the rotors off the wheels, and unplug the Shimano Di2 battery before packing everything securely. I stash my helmet (in it’s case) and shoes in the bike bag, slide bottles into the cages, and always drop an Apple AirTag in there-just in case I need to track it along the way.

The only carbon on the bike is the wheels-everything else is rock solid. That gives me total confidence every time I throw a leg over, knowing it’s all in working order and ready to roll.

I travel a lot for my work with USA Cycling and for events around the country, and let’s be honest-bike travel can be a pain. But Moots takes a lot of that stress off my shoulders. It’s just one of those brands that makes you feel like you’re part of something solid. No squeaks, creaks, no fuss, just smooth riding and peace of mind.

Traveling with a Moots means I always have a little piece of home with me-no matter the airport, the hotel, or the back of a rental car. And for someone who’s constantly on the move with her bike, that’s priceless.

This spring and summer, my Vamoots RCS is hitting the road again. I’ll be taking it to San Francisco in April multiple times, then to the mountains of West Virginia for the USA Cycling Road National Championships, where I’ll be commentating the elite races on FloBikes. And later this summer, it’s off to Annecy, France for our USA Cycling Foundation trip to watch the Tour de France Femmes avec Zwift-one of the highlight trips of the summer!

Wherever the calendar takes me next, I know my Moots is ready. And honestly, that makes the travel easier for me- more peace of mind, and more excitement about the destinations and the chance to ride with my cycling community.

If you have more questions about traveling wiht your Moots please reachout and we can guide you with recommendations. Stay tuned for the next Lauren Hall blog in May...

entry.title: Winter Miles & Community Vibes – Tucson Cycling
entry.content:
There’s something special about Tucson, AZ – a place where the sun always seems to shine, the roads are made for riding, and the cycling community feels like family. For the past eight years or so, this has been one of my go-to training locations, offering everything from fast -paced group rides to long solo miles on wide-open roads. It’s a place that keeps calling me back, and for good reason.

One of the best ways to experience Tucson’s cycling culture is the legendary Shootout, a Saturday morning group ride that brings together riders of all levels- from weekend warriors to World Tour and Gravel pros. It’s a staple in the cycling world, a true test of fitness, and one of the best ways to push yourself while soaking in the energy of the local riding scene.

Beyond the Shootout, Tucson offers endless options for both challenging and relaxed rides. The Loop provides over 130 miles of car-free riding, perfect for easy spins or recovery days. And then there’s Mt. Lemmon -an iconic, nearly 7,000-foot climb that rewards riders with epic views. Gates Pass is another favorite, offering one of the most stunning ride experiences in town.

And what better way to enjoy these roads than on my Moots Vamoots RCS? The smooth titanium ride, responsive handling, and all-day comfort make it the perfect companion for Tucson’s terrain.

Giving Back: Tucson Bicycle Classic

 

 

For the past four years, I’ve had the privilege of helping with the Tucson Bicycle Classic, a race that has become an incredible launching pad for new women racers. The turnout was fantastic and seeing so many new faces on the start line was inspiring. Supporting women’s racing has always been close to my heart, and Tucson continues to be a place where the cycling community truly steps up to make the sport more inclusive and exciting.

Coming Up…

While I’ve been soaking up all that Tucson has to offer, I’m also gearing up for some exciting events. Next stops: Monterey, CA for the Sea Otter Classic, San Francisco for the Climate Ride on April 22nd

If you’re in the area, I’d love to connect, ride, and talk about how USA Cycling Foundation is supporting the next generation of cyclists!

Tucson has reminded me once again why I love this sport-it’s about more than just the miles. It’s the people, the places, and the experiences that make cycling such a powerful and lifelong passion.

See you on the road!

entry.title: Finding My Way Back: A Journey of Resilience and Discovery of Moots Express
entry.content:
Twenty-two years ago, my life changed forever during a national level mountain bike race in Big Bear, California. As an aspiring mountain biker pushing my limits during a practice run, I suffered a devastating crash that left me with a spinal cord injury. The prognosis was stark: a single-digit chance of walking again.

In the ICU, heavily sedated, I stared at the ceiling as my mind spiraled through an endless loop of regret. The pain was unlike anything I’d ever experienced—deep, relentless. But the physical agony was matched by the mental anguish of uncertainty about my future. The doctors' words echoed like a death sentence: "Mr. Takaki, you won't be able to walk again and you need to adapt to a new life." With my spine fused with rods and almost no chance of walking again, I felt my sense of control over my body and future slipping away. My self-esteem plummeted to the darkest corner I'd ever known, and initially, I gave up on my life entirely.

But from that moment on, my journey became one of continuous small victories, each building on the last. From the first flicker of movement in my right toe two weeks after the accident to learning to stand, walk, and cross a busy street on my own—each milestone wasn’t just physical progress, but a reclaiming of independence.

Yet the emotional terrain I had to navigate was even gnarlier than any mountain bike trail I’d ever encountered. At first, I did my best to hide it,masking my insecurities with the determination to overcome this life altering event. For two years, confined to a wheelchair, I wrestled with a storm of denial, anger, and crushing hopelessness. The contrast was staggering—one day, I was racing down an adrenaline-fueled downhill course, pushing my limits; the next, I was paralyzed from the waist down, struggling to roll over a simple five-inch curb. Basic tasks that had once been second nature—walking, showering, getting dressed—became distant memories rather than the routine actions I had once taken for granted.

But even in the darkest moments, something familiar emerged. As I wheeled myself a little further each day, testing and pushing my boundaries, I recognized the same spirit that had drawn me to cycling as a child—the instinct to explore, to see what lay beyond my current limits. The first time I ventured outside the hospital on my own in a wheelchair, it felt like seeing an ocean for the first time—vast, unknown, and exhilarating. In reality, I had only wheeled 20 feet from the door, but in my mind, I had crossed into something far greater: a new challenge, a new thrill, a new kind of freedom. This wasn’t just recovery; it was the ultimate test of my willingness to face a challenge head-on, to embrace the struggle rather than retreat from it. I was fortunate to regain movement early on, and that gave me enormous hope and motivation—something that became the foundation of my mental strength. When there is light, it can always get brighter. That realization fueled my determination, helping me push past my insecurities and build the resilience I needed.

And I wasn’t alone on this journey. Friends and family anchored me through the storm, offering unwavering support as I processed my new reality. I’ll never forget the day my closest riding buddy showed up at rehab, bringing with him a super burrito—it was spicy, and to my dismay, packed with beans (I hate beans). But somehow, that burrito instantly transported me back to better days. We sat there for hours, not with pity, but with patience, swapping stories of recent rides and future adventures. Their presence became the foundation that helped me push through the mental fog of depression and loss of identity.

Later, my cycling community reinforced that support in ways only they could—riding alongside me on the climbs, never making me feel like a burden, and reminding me that the ride isn’t just about speed but about showing up, pushing through, and sharing the journey together. Their quiet patience and encouragement kept me moving forward, proving that I was never truly riding alone.

The path back to cycling wasn’t immediate or straightforward. Every small victory in physical therapy felt monumental—sitting up independently, taking those first assisted steps while strapped into what felt like an exoskeleton, balancing long enough to dress myself. With every session, my body slowly responded, and my relationship with movement evolved from struggle to possibility.

My return to cycling began modestly. From a wheelchair to an e-scooter, then finally to a pedal bike—at first, just 5 miles at a time. I found a new rhythm in simple routines: daily swims recommended by my doctor, short bike rides to the pool and grocery store. These small journeys might have seemed insignificant to others, but to me—remembering those dark days in the ICU—they were nothing short of miraculous.

The first time I pedaled across the Golden Gate Bridge toward the top of Hawk Hill, I knew it would be a test—not just of my strength, but of my mindset. I had mentally prepared for this ride, but the moment I hit the first steep section, exhilaration quickly gave way to exhaustion. I was pushing my limit, and yet, I was barely moving. Riders of all kinds—weekend warriors, tourists, even a little kid—passed me effortlessly. My ego took a hit, but in that moment, I told myself: It doesn’t matter how others see me. My happiness is what matters most.

Reaching the top, breathless and spent, I was met with a view that made every struggle worth it—the vast expanse of San Francisco Bay stretching beyond the bridge, blue sky reflecting off the water. It was one of my happiest moments, a reminder that effort, not speed, is what truly defines the ride. What started as a single test of willpower became the foundation for something bigger. Little by little, I kept expanding my horizons—short trips to the pool, then to the store, then beyond. What began as a means of recovery gradually evolved into something more—a return not just to cycling, but to regaining my independence.

From then on, I shifted my focus. I set incremental, realistic goals so that even when I fell short, progress always felt within reach. And as I kept pushing, those small wins added up. There was a profound beauty in this simplicity. Each pedal stroke carried me further from who I had been in that hospital bed and closer to who I could become. I took my time, expanding my horizons with each ride, finding freedom in those small adventures. In the end, it all came down to living life on my own terms.

Then COVID hit, disrupting the careful routine I’d built. The pool where I’d spent countless hours strengthening my body shut down indefinitely. What could have been a setback became an unexpected catalyst. Searching for a new way to stay active, I discovered lightweight e-gravel bikes—a revelation. Suddenly, the boundaries I’d grown accustomed to began to dissolve. My limited range stretched to 40-50 miles. The Golden Gate Bridge, the Marin Headlands where I first fell in love with cycling after moving from Japan in 1996—all were within reach again. Even Mount Tamalpais, the birthplace of mountain biking, felt challenging again.

The bike transformed from just a mode of transportation into something much deeper—it became my gateway to freedom and connection. Each component spoke to me of adaptation and possibility: the battery fueling my adventures, the dropper post enabling me to mount, and the suspension fork and tire inserts giving me the confidence to tackle challenging terrain again. These weren’t just bike parts; they were the foundation of my independence.

Though I still walk with a cane, something magical happens when I swing my leg over the saddle. On the bike, the limitations I face on foot seem to melt into the wind. Especially on descents, when gravity takes over and the trail opens up—those are the moments when everything else fades away. The familiar rush of speed returns, the bike responds intuitively, and I’m no longer the guy with the cane. I’m just another rider, carving through the trail, chasing that perfect line. My happiness was stripped away in an instant the day of the accident, but through years of rehab, my joy for the sport has returned.

As these moments of freedom grew, so did my ambitions. The more I rode, the more I dreamed of pushing beyond my limits—exploring trails I once thought were out of reach. Each ride hinted at new adventures, calling me toward possibilities I hadn’t even imagined.

As my confidence grew, so did my desire to explore further. Along the way, I found myself surrounded by a growing circle of riding friends, each one encouraging me to push a little more, try a new trail, or join a longer adventure. Yet my reality was different. Because I needed more power assist to compensate for my weaker legs, my battery drained faster, limiting my range no matter how much I wanted to keep going. The combination of battery range and my physical strength often meant having to decline invitations or turn back while others rode on. Those 50-mile adventures left me wondering—what else might be possible? Familiar routes began to feel less like destinations and more like boundaries. I found myself dreaming of longer rides, more challenging terrain, and the opportunity to experience new horizons alongside my friends. What once was a pessimistic outlook on the constrictions I had with limited movement has now transformed into optimism through exceeding previous plateaus and reaching new heights.

By the time I entered my third year of riding a lightweight e-gravel bike, I started to have a clearer sense of what I truly needed from my setup. I realized I needed more range for longer rides, the capacity for larger tires to increase comfort and traction, and although not absolutely necessary, a bit more motor power to help me tackle steep sections with greater ease and safety. Reflecting on these needs, it became clear that I was searching for something more tailored to my evolving journey—something that could push the boundaries of what I thought was beyond my reach.

Sometimes, discoveries find you in unexpected ways. My discovery path to the Moots Express began at the Sea Otter Classic, where a few unexpected conversations set everything in motion. A friend from Ornot, the San Francisco-based cycling apparel brand, spoke with the president of Moots and later sent me an excited message about the bike. Around the same time, someone at Shimano who I’d met the previous year through my connections had already mentioned my name to Moots, encouraging them to keep an eye on me.

Moots didn’t just check off the boxes—they built the Express for big adventures from the start. More than just specs on paper, every design choice translated into real benefits on the trail. The suspension-ready frame and larger tires didn’t just improve comfort; they gave me the confidence to push my limits, knowing my bike could handle whatever lay ahead. In the Express, I saw more than just a bike. I saw the perfect tool to unlock the next chapter of my riding journey.

What really sealed my decision to get the Moots Express was the complete Shimano integration. The responsive EP801 motor and the Linkglide drivetrain with its Freeshift technology allowed me to tackle tough descents and punchy climbs with ease, letting me conserve energy and stay engaged. After years of riding a modified bike, I found the Moots Express to be purpose-built for durability and long-distance adventures. The trust I have in Shimano’s reliability for parts and service gives me confidence that this bike will be a companion for many miles to come.

Before the Moots Express, I had ridden a similar bike—a carbon gravel e-bike—but the difference in ride quality and performance was striking. The Moots Express isn’t just a bike; it’s a partner in this journey of discovery, delivering the capability and excitement I was looking for.

The new bike’s geometry, combined with the ability to run larger tires, allows me to pick lines with confidence and ride all day without discomfort. The higher cockpit, modern geometry, and quick battery swap feature are just a few of the thoughtful details that make the Moots Express feel like a perfect fit for my adventures ahead.

For a deeper dive into the technical specs and what makes this bike truly stand out, stay tuned for the next blog where I’ll break down the detailed features of my Moots Express dream build.

Through sharing my story, I've connected with new friends and communities that encourage me to expand my horizons. Their support and shared belief in growth through change continue to inspire me to reach beyond what I once thought was possible.

Each ride now serves as a testament to what’s possible. From that hospital room, where walking seemed impossible, to today, where I’m exploring trails I never thought I’d see again—it’s no longer about distance or speed. It’s about the pure joy of being on a bike, feeling the wind rush by, and realizing that with each ride, I'm expanding what I once thought was beyond my reach.

The Moots Express isn't just a bike; it’s become a partner in this journey of discovery. Looking ahead, I see countless trails and adventures, because sometimes the end of one path is just the beginning of another—and with every ride, it’s a reminder that new horizons are waiting to be explored.

In the coming weeks Saboo will share more with our readers around his build and other inspiration - follow him on instagram: iam.fooski

entry.title: Apacheria Gravel: A First-Year Cycling Adventure with the Moots Routt RSL
entry.content:
There's something special about supporting a first-year cycling event-it's a testament to people's love and passion for this sport. On November 16, I participated in the inaugural Apacheria Gravel event in Douglas, Arizona. Organized with heart and grit, this event embodied the spirit of adventure that makes gravel cycling unique.

A Fresh Start with a New Companion

The Apacheria Gravel event was only the second time I'd ridden my new Moots Routt RSL. I picked it up in Steamboat Springs back in early October, greeted by the golden hues of changing leaves and the warm hospitality of the Moots family. Nate gave me a thorough rundown of the bike's features, and I left Steamboat with excitement and anticipation for the adventures ahead. Life and work kept me busy, leaving little time to bond with the bike before the event. But as soon as I threw my leg over the Routt for the 66-mile distance, all concerns melted away. The bike is a masterpiece-responsive yet forgiving, with geometry that perfectly balances a racy feel and all-day comfort. The 44mm WTB tires were a game-changer, soaking up the rough terrain and providing a smooth, comfortable ride that kept me fresh all day.

A Day to Remember

The route was challenging and beautiful, showcasing the rugged landscapes of southern Arizona and a stout headwind on the way home. Surrounded by friends from the Tucson cycling community, the day was filled with camaraderie, laughter, and a shared passion for the sport. To top it all off, I stood on the podium's top step- a sweet bonus to an already unforgettable experience.

Gratitude for the Moots Family

Reflecting on the day, I couldn't be more grateful for my Routt RSL and the Moots family. They've created a bike that performs and connects me to the adventures I hold dear. Since Apacheria, the Routt has been my partner for more rides and new explorations, and I'm excited to see where it will take me next. Thank you to everyone who poured their heart into making Apacheria Gravel a success. And to my Moots family, your support means the world to me. Here's to more first-year events, unforgettable rides, and new memories on bikes.

entry.title: New Bike Day - Moots Trade-Up Program!
entry.content:
It’s true, we build bicycles to last a lifetime. There’s no doubt that many of the beloved products we’ve produced since 1981 still make riders smile, 20 and 30 years later. And while Moots owners will tell you they absolutely love their bike, some are curious about how a new premium tubeset, a new geometry, disc brakes, more tire clearance, or an updated parts kit would bring them an entirely new riding joy!

Introducing our “Trade-Up” program - a way for us at Moots to acknowledge the love you have for your bike, and to share our passion of chasing perfection with new bike designs, materials, and updated technology.

We offer Moots owners an opportunity to turn their existing, rideable frame, into a $2,000 credit towards a complete bike direct from your local Moots dealer or directly from Moots.

This program applies whether you’re the original owner, or not. There are no model or production year restrictions!

 

How it works:

  1. Inspect your frame - it must be free of cracked welds or large dents. (FYI - There’s a second, detailed inspection later in the process, so be diligent!)

  2. Go into your local dealer and speak to a sales representative about the Moots tradeup program. Our dealers are dialed in on the tradeup program and will walk you down the path of your next Moots. Please see our dealer locator to identify a dealer in your area. If there is not a dealer nearby, we are always here for and you can reach us at tradeup@moots.com.

  3. We’ll have a look and give you the thumbs up to ship us your bike. Or we’ll explain why we’re unable to offer you a credit.

  4. Ship us your frame (or complete bike - see FAQ below)

  5. We’ll communicate receipt of your bike and status of your credit via email. Once everything is inspected, we’ll apply your $2,000 credit at the close of purchase of your new bike - if your bike doesn't qualify for the program,

    we'll ship it back to you at our cost. 

Ship to:

 

Moots - TradeUp

 

2545 Copper Ridge Dr

 

Steamboat Springs, CO80487

FAQ

If I send my complete bike, will I get the parts back?

  • No! If you want to keep your parts kit (wheels, drivetrain, brakes, etc.), the frame should be stripped. We will not disassemble your bike and return your parts. We will not disassemble your bike and hold your parts for you to come pick up. Whatever you send us, we're assuming you'll never want to see it again! There is no going back on this so please take time to consider your future wants!

What if I’m not the original owner?

  • Not a problem, we don’t require any receipts or paperwork to credit you towards your purchase of a new complete bike.

Can I trade in my frame for cash?

  • This program is designed to reward passionate Moots fans. The aim is to offer a credit towards an updated model for the “refresh button” on ride experiences…sorry, no cash value.

Do I have to purchase a complete bike?

  • Yeah, that’s the deal. No sugar coating here.

My bike is worth more than $2,000 in the used bike market - will Moots give me more credit?

  • If your bike is worth more than the $2,000 we offer, we encourage you to look to reputable 3rd-party marketplaces like TPC and Bicycle Blue Book to get the most of your bike. Also check with your local retailer to see if they have a used bike program. We can only hope you’ll put that scratch towards a new Moots!

Does this program apply if I want to buy a Moots from my local shop?

  • Yes!

    Moots retailers are the backbone of our 43-year heritage! If you love your local Moots dealer,

    they can share the program details and you can purchase your new Moots locally.

    They can email tradeup@moots.com, or talk to their sales rep. Regardless if you work with us directly, or your local retailer, the Moots Trade-Up program only applies to complete bike purchases.

Can this credit be applied to a frame or frameset?

  • At the moment, the $2,000 credit applies to complete bike purchases only. As this program evolves over time, we’ll explore how it might include frame and frameset purchases.

Am I guaranteed credit?

  • There are no guarantees in life! But if you did a good job inspecting your frame and there are no cracks or large dents….yeah, it’s pretty much a sure thing! If we communicate that we can’t offer you a credit, there will be a very clear reason why. We truly want riders on our latest and greatest bikes and will do everything we can to make that happen! And, we'll ship it back to you.

Does this program apply to Express eBike models?

  • Of course! A Moots is a Moots! The goal is to support our dedicated fan base with bikes they love and want, and we’re stoked to have two incredible ebikes to offer!

I see there are closeout bikes on the Moots site, can I use this credit towards the purchase of a discounted bike?

  • No, this offer only applies to new orders and is not applicable to any items that have already been discounted.

What happens to my Moots once it’s been accepted for the Trade Up program?

  • Some of the Trade Up bikes end up in our museum here in Steamboat Springs, Colorado. Others get refurbished and are placed in retail partner locations, or collaboration projects with some of our favorite companies. In short, they tell a story that can be shared across the world!

entry.title: From Pro Peloton to the Moots Family: My Journey on and Off the Bike
entry.content:
Hi, Moots family! I'm Lauren Hall, a former professional cyclist, lifelong athlete, and proud Moots ambassador. As someone who's spent years chasing finish lines and now thrives on exploring new roads and trails, I couldn't be more excited to share my story with you.

A Little About Me

Growing up in Vicksburg, Mississippi, I was an all-around athlete, playing soccer, basketball, tennis, and running track. My passion for competition earned me a full scholarship to play soccer at Mississippi State University, where I graduated in 2001. After college, I explored different paths, from culinary school to managing child nutrition programs, before discovering cycling at 28 – a little late by traditional standards but just in time to find my true calling. Cycling became my world, and soon, I found myself racing professionally for eight years. During that time, I raced for teams like Optum, United Healthcare, and Team Twenty16, competed in four World Championships, and proudly represented the U.S. National Team in Europe for three seasons. One of my career highlights? Winning a spring classic, Gent-Wevelgem, in 2014- a victory that still feels surreal.

Why Moots?

After retiring from the professional peloton, I sought a bike that would reconnect me with the pure joy of riding, my forever bike. Moots bikes have always been synonymous with craftsmanship, performance, timeless design, and the titanium frame needed with my current travel – all points that resonate deeply with me. When Moots provided me with a Vamoots RCS, equipped with Shimano Dura-Ace, HED Vanquish 45 Pro wheels, and aluminum bars (my choice), it reignited my love for exploring roads less traveled. That bike wasn't just a tool; it became an extension of my passion for riding. I've embraced a new cycling medium with a new Moots Routt RSL gravel bike decked out with SRAM Force, HED wheels, WTB 44 tires, and ENVE bars. Gravel riding has been an exciting way to explore new places and create fresh adventures. It's taken me off the beaten path, offering a sense of freedom and discovery that feels different from my road racing days. From quiet backroads to rugged trails, this bike has opened up endless opportunities for adventure and exploration.

What's Next?

Through this blog series, I'll share stories from my days in the pro peloton, my transition to life off the bike, and how Moots inspires my adventures today. Beyond the bike, I work for the USA Cycling Foundation, where I have the privilege of contributing to the mission of supporting athletes and the sport. This role allows me to be part of some incredible experiences, from attending the men's and women's Tour de France trips to cheering on our U.S. athletes at Road World Championships, Olympics and events across the U.S. Additionally, I've taken on a commentating role for marquee events like the Life Time Grand Prix series (see the YouTube series), SBT GRVL, and more. It's a dynamic and exciting way to stay connected to the sport and community that have shaped my life. -Lauren

Join us monthly as Lauren details her transition from the pro peloton to her now impactful roll in the gravel community.

entry.title: Embracing Innovation: Moots' Transition to UDH-Compatible Frames
entry.content:
Let's talk about something buzzing in the biking world, UDH, Universal Derailleur Hanger. At first glance, it might seem like just another component, but recently, it's become much more.

Thanks to SRAM's recent transmission innovations, T-Type, and now called Full-Mount, UDH is quickly becoming the must-have feature for every serious rider. Are you curious about what all these fancy terms mean and how they impact your Moots riding experience? Follow along, and we'll break it all down.


UNDERSTANDING UDH, FULL MOUNT, AND T-TYPE FROM SRAM

This is our timeline of the SRAM component introductions. Disclaimer: The timeline or naming may not be perfect, but it's how we recall it!

2019 - SRAM introduced UDH to the world, designing a derailleur hanger to simplify maintenance for all riders by having one standard that every bike can use worldwide.

2023 - SRAM introduced Eagle Transmission, T-Type, a drivetrain system that no longer bolts onto a derailleur hanger, but the derailleur/transmission attaches directly to the frame using the same interface as the UDH.

2024 - SRAM introduced the RED XPLR 13-speed gravel groupset. Transmission/T-Type was renamed to Full Mount. Full Mount is essentially the same as the prior Eagle Transmission, using the UDH frame interface to mount the derailleur directly to the frame and bypassing the use of a derailleur hanger.

UDH is compatible with SRAM's Full Mount drivetrain line-up, including the Eagle Transmission and RED XPLR AXS groupsets. Full Mount derailleurs work around the rear axle's center, optimizing shift performance and eliminating unnecessary parts.


I CAME HERE TO HEAR ABOUT MOOTS

Ok, here is what we have been doing here at Moots:

July 2023 - Introduction of the Routt CRD, our first UDH-compatible frame.

January 2024 - Womble, Mountaineer, and Forager all were revised to be UDH compatible.

April 2024 - MXC was introduced as a new model in the XC/adventure MTB sector of the model line-up…obviously with UDH-compatible dropouts.

June 2024 - Routt RSL redesigned to include several updates, one being UDH compatibility.

October 2024 - Routt 45 and Routt YBB reworked to incorporate UDH-compatible dropouts.

Moots may have "taken our time" adapting the UDH interface into our frames. We wish we could've moved faster, but it's not simple! Aside from the three-year bike boom, when everything went well, a few other things slowed our progress in making the transition.

We have always, and will continue, to make practical decisions to enhance the ride characteristics of a titanium bike with all of our design choices. UDH is complicated from a metal bike perspective. Essentially, 7.1mm of the driveside dropout goes away and becomes part of either the hanger or the derailleur. This means the titanium dropouts, in this case, are asymmetric from the center line of the frame and balanced out in the end by the hanger or derailleur. When we set out to build a frame, every step throughout production focuses on creating a dead, straight frame for the end user. Balancing and managing the offset all the way through took time to retool and develop unique processes that we had never done before.

Prior to UDH, the average thickness of our replaceable derailleur hangers was around 7mm. A UDH has a cross-section of 20mm. Our team and partners worked on creating dropout designs that elegantly accommodated the interface, but not all made it past the early design phase.

So, what does this mean? All Moots MTB & Gravel bikes are now available with UDH-compatible dropouts.

GREAT! WHAT DOES THIS MEAN FOR THE MOOTS THAT I ALREADY OWN?

We understand that many of our loyal customers own non-UDH frames, and we want to assure you that your bikes remain a testament to our commitment to quality and craftsmanship. Each Moots bike, regardless of the derailleur hanger system, is designed with intention, precision, and a deep appreciation for the art of hand-building bikes. We will continue to manufacture and supply hangers for our previous models.

Whether you're riding a well-loved classic or one of our latest models, know that your Moots bike is built to perform and inspire countless adventures. Our journey is about creating exceptional experiences for every rider, and we're excited to continue this journey with you.

entry.title: New Mexico: The Land of Enchantment & Very Sore Legs
entry.content:
Occasionally, I like to find a feat of strength that helps me decompress from life. The harder the feat, the more I gain confidence and the ability to return to the mundane absurdity of my life. This feat was significantly more epic than anything I'd ever attempted. Six days riding from Santa Fe, NM, to Las Cruces, NM, most of which would be off-road. Winter arrived early in New Mexico this year to make things more interesting. Forty-eight hours before the start of the ride, New Mexico received two feet of snow along the route followed the first three days. And when we made it out of the snow, the cold remained. Most of the other days started with temperatures in the high teens. Suffice it to say, this feat of strength nearly killed me, but it was totally worth it. This ride was what I needed this year. Sometimes, when you go past the limits you thought you had, nothing is impossible. I'm lucky to have friends who push me to ride harder and go further than I'd ever go on my own, and it's changed my life. I'm also fortunate my wife introduced me to Moots in the mid-2000s. Moots is the real reason I can ride further, harder, and more efficiently than ever. When a friend proposed this ride, I knew it was the perfect opportunity to get my friends Colin and Jonathan of ACME Bicycle Company NYC to design me a new Routt CRD. Doing so remotely added more of a challenge, but it will be okay with a fit team this good. ACME designed me a rocket ship and fit me perfectly to the high-performance edge I'd need to keep up with the excellent team members I'd be riding alongside for the week. I selected some super fast 40MM ZIPP XPLR SLICK tires to easily keep up with the boys on the road sections. This tire selection proved more insane as we approached the multiple national wildlife refuges along the route. Luckily, I brought my legacy rig and my beloved Baxter monster gravel bike for the more single-track sections. It was an absolute blast bombing down frozen National Forest Service roads in the middle of nowhere on this rig. The Baxter did NOT care! The sheer beauty of New Mexico was truly overwhelming. Getting to experience this beauty on a brand new Routt CRD and with the most incredible group of guys was one of the most powerful moments I've experienced as a rider. Every day brought more stunning parts of a country I'd never imagined existed. Every day, we met more interesting New Mexicans along the route at food and drink stops or while pausing on a totally remote dirt road. This route was as much a test of riding strength as the ability to reconnect with America! And on both accounts, it was simply fantastic. It isn't easy to pinpoint my favorite part of this trek because it was the most meticulously planned and stunning 500 miles I'd ever ridden linked together. However, if I had to choose one, the most beautiful part of this ride was our day in the Cibola National Forest. It was a chilly start to the day, but I barely noticed it because the National Forest was so breathtaking. After a stretch of tarmac, we turned onto a fire road and rode across the vast array of twenty-eight 25-meter radio telescopes on railroad tracks. As I climbed to the peak that would drop me over the Sierra Ladrones and onto the road to our evening stop in Magdalena, I noticed I was following giant bear tracks up the mountain. I thought to myself, "That's about right." I hurt so bad and was so high on endorphins from the previous days and miles it seemed perfectly reasonable that there was a chance I'd now have to fight a bear to the death to reach my final destination for the day. Luckily, my bear friend was long gone when I reached the top. I finished this ride with a newfound respect for my friends, a new appreciation for how to train, and a madly in love with the new Routt CRD. The Routt CRD is the ultimate gravel weapon, and I look forward to training on this rig this offseason to prepare for the 2025 race season. Thanks to this bike, guaranteed personal bests will fall, and I will achieve even more. If you are considering this rig, call me, and I'll tell you what it can do!

BIKE DEETS:

2024 ROUTT CRD

1X SRAM RED EXPLORO

ZIPP 303 XPLR WHEELSET

MOOTS GRAVEL BAR

ZIPP XPLORO SLICK 40MM TIRES
